CPU_train50k_audit.provenance: Preparation-time CPU audit copied to Colab results; not repeated by this run or the current analysis.

interpretation: A AMP batch128 + bucketing + fused AdamW is the fastest completed training throughput candidate under both 14e9-byte peak limits.
B AMP batch128 completed with finite losses, zero measured skipped updates and 13.495 GB peak reserved; limited memory headroom.
A FP32 batch128 completed but reserved14.365 GB exceeds the predetermined threshold.
A AMP batch8 is slower than the same-run FP32 batch8 control. This does not extend to larger batches.
Sorted FP16 batch512 is fastest greedy inference: 190/991, versus control189/991; 998/1024 heldout and1860/1919 test token-identical.
All sorted FP32 variants are fully token-identical to control; batch128 is the fastest FP32 variant.
All new CPU execution matches reproduce saved Colab execution exactly; new model updates and GPU measurements are zero.
limits: Throughput uses newly initialized short-run models; it does not establish quality or convergence speed for batch128 or models B/C.
Only9/20 train configs completed. Five OOMs; C has12 warmup steps in one config and five configs not started due reserved phase budget.
Batch, bucketing and fused AdamW changed together in the main grid; compare FP32/AMP on identical batch plans to isolate precision.
Inference uses fixed22/100k weights, greedy cap512, one timing repetition per variant. No beam or sampling.
Full wall includes load, restoration, warmup, generation and answer-file writing; excludes HF download, caching and exec scoring.
The one/two extra exec matches with FP16 are not significant (paired exact McNemar p1.0/0.5).
FP16 changes some sequences despite preserved exec-match; test has no official quality labels.
Observed SDPA operator is efficient_attention for profiled shapes; enabled flash flag does not establish FlashAttention use.
Fresh heldout1024 remains unscored; official bot file format and official leaderboard score remain unknown.
